questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses in English as well as meeting a culture which would both inspire and challenge me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found some things quite difficult

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some complications upon my arrival, for example a national strike affecting the uni's opening hours, and I felt communication could have been clearer to ensure a comfortable arrival. Instead, they prioritized handing out gif bags full of things nobody needs. It would have been much more appreciated to receive more comprehensive information about timetables for courses, campuses, how to get proof of attendance signed, who to reach out to in terms of issues with classes, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. Cannot recommend the two different places I lived as they were expensive and not in great shape

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Book for the first few weeks in advance - find permanent housing once you're there

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I remember, it went pretty smoothly

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was sent an email with info from Ca' Foscari

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful - but I ended up investing a lot of time researching on my own to figure it out

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take one step at a time. Make a checklist to feel progress and keep track of steps

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the selection of courses in English completely satisfying. However, I found some of the courses I took were not academically up to par with a Master's degree - for example I experienced that one course didn't have an actual syllabus, only the professor's slides

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As mentioned, I found some of the courses I took were not academically up to par with a Master's degree - for example I experienced that one course didn't have an actual syllabus, only the professor's slides

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I am used to more student participation and analytical engagement at UCPH. At Ca' Foscari I found that simply memorizing facts was the valued skill in most cases

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: City tours. And I believe there were running clubs, food classes, group trips, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in anything but the tour of Venice - it was a good opportunity to get aquatinted with the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Padova, Verona, Valpolicella, Garda, Bologna, Milano, Prosecco, Slovenia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had mixed experiences

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to people in your class - they're probably just as interested in new friends, and as nervous, as you are

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I struggled with the laidbackness of the culture as I prefer planning and getting things in order weeks or months in advance. I also struggled with the bluntness which I found to be rude at times

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outside of Venice people are usually quite hospitable, excellent food and wine

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find permanent accommodation after you arrive
Quickly ally yourself with other exchange students so you can >exchange< complaints and fears - it reduces anxiety
Take advantage of Venice's location - visit other good spots by train, the mountains, Bologna, etc.
Don't take rudeness personally

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Exams start really late compared to most other unis. Maybe pick somewhere else if you want to be back home by the time your next semester begins at your sending uni.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot of new insights about myself, my needs, my character and my life. I gained new appreciation for everything waiting for me back home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness (/longing for home) and uncertainty/some unease becomes a part of your daily life

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
